title: Which is the smallest square that 4, 9 and 10 all divide?
description: The primes of four, nine and ten are gathered into one smallest number, then the primes left without a partner are paired up. The answer is put back into the question to check it.
teaching_notes: One idea: build the smallest common multiple from primes, then give every prime a partner. Watch for students who stop at one hundred eighty because it is divisible by all three numbers.

video_script.why: The child uses the pairing of primes from the solved example to build the smallest square divisible by three numbers.
video_script.substitution: Gather the primes of four, nine and ten, then multiply by whatever prime has no partner.
video_script.anchor: the three numbers four, nine and ten written on cards
video_script.payoff_line: The smallest square number is nine hundred

final_answer.spoken: the smallest square number is nine hundred

video_script.design: One idea: pair every prime. The three cards stay in the anchor band and the prime lines sit on the working board.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; three number cards, 4, 9 and 10, in the anchor band, with the words smallest square number? under them

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.nums: the three number cards 4, 9 and 10 appear
marks.ask: the words smallest square number? appear under the cards

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='nums'/>It gives three numbers, four, nine and ten.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which is the smallest square number that all three of them divide?

beats.on_screen: the three cards hold still and the words smallest square number? glow

marks.stop: the words smallest square number? glow in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a row of coloured prime tiles; matching tiles join in pairs, and a tile without a match flashes

marks.pairs: matching prime tiles join in pairs
marks.left: a tile without a match flashes

narration: <bookmark mark='pairs'/>In a square number, every prime has a partner.
<bookmark mark='left'/>We will gather the primes of the three numbers, then find the ones left alone.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the numbers are four, nine and ten.

beats.on_screen: To find: the smallest square number divisible by 4, 9 and 10

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the smallest square number that all three divide.

marks.primes: the three prime lines are written one under the other

narration: <bookmark mark='primes'/>Step one, write each number as primes.
Four is two times two, nine is three times three, and ten is two times five.

beats.on_screen: smallest number with all of them inside: 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 = 180

marks.need: the primes needed are gathered into one line
marks.val: = 180 is written at the end of the line

narration: <bookmark mark='need'/>Step two, gather the primes the smallest number needs.
It needs two twos for four, two threes for nine, and one five for ten.
<bookmark mark='val'/>Two times two times three times three times five is one hundred eighty.

beats.on_screen: 180 × 5 = 900, and 900 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 × 5; the twos, the threes and the fives are all in pairs

marks.alone: the 5 in 180 flashes because it has no partner
marks.times: × 5 is written, giving 900 and the prime line with two 5s
marks.pairs: all the primes join in pairs

narration: <bookmark mark='alone'/>Step three, find the prime without a partner.
The twos and the threes are in pairs, but the five is alone.
<bookmark mark='times'/>Multiply by five, which gives nine hundred.
<bookmark mark='pairs'/>Every prime in this number has a partner.

beats.on_screen: put the answer back in the question: 900 ÷ 4 = 225, 900 ÷ 9 = 100, 900 ÷ 10 = 90

marks.back: 900 is put back next to the numbers 4, 9 and 10
marks.ok: each division gives a whole number and is ticked

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step four, put the answer back in the question.
Nine hundred shared by four is two hundred twenty five.
<bookmark mark='ok'/>Nine hundred shared by nine is one hundred, and shared by ten is ninety.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Nine hundred is thirty times thirty, so it is a square.
The smallest square number is nine hundred.
